☀ Solar-assisted • Lightweight • Vendor-first

A smarter street cart for everyday India.

EcoMule reimagines the rugged utility vehicle as a lightweight electric vegetable cart: easy to drive, inexpensive to run, shaded by solar panels, and designed to transform into a comfortable selling station when parked.

Modular frameRepairable and configurable

Built around the vendor.

Instead of shrinking a conventional vehicle, EcoMule starts with the real needs of a mobile street seller: visibility, storage, shade, low running cost, easy access and quick transition from driving to selling.

☀️

Solar canopy

The roof creates shade while supplying auxiliary power for lights, charging, display electronics and battery top-up.

🪶

Lightweight frame

A tubular aluminium or high-strength steel chassis keeps the vehicle simple, repairable and easier to move through narrow streets.

🔋

Electric assist

Low-speed electric drive reduces physical strain and makes daily neighbourhood routes more practical.

🧺

Modular produce bays

Crates stay accessible from the customer side and can be removed quickly for loading, sorting and cleaning.

⚖️

Integrated selling tools

A weighing scale, price display, storage tray, task lighting and payment/phone mount can live directly on the cart.

🔧

Local-service friendly

Standard wheels, exposed frame sections and simple panels make the concept easier to maintain without specialised bodywork.

↻ Signature feature

One seat. Two jobs.

The driver’s chair sits on a lockable swivel base. While moving, it faces forward with access to the steering and controls. Once parked and secured, the vendor releases the lock, rotates the chair toward the produce and customers, and locks it again.

Drive mode

Face forward

Seat locked toward the controls for safe low-speed driving and clear road visibility.

Sell mode

Turn toward customers

Rotate the chair after parking so the vendor can sit naturally beside the produce without climbing out.

Concept architecture.

These are design-direction targets rather than final engineering specifications. They make the idea concrete enough for prototyping and cost studies.

RoofIntegrated solar canopy
SeatLockable swivel base
CargoRemovable produce crates
Retail toolsScale, price board, lights, phone/payment mount

Why this form works

A vegetable vendor often spends more time stationary than driving. That means the vehicle should behave less like a tiny truck and more like a movable shop.

Design principle:
Drive like a utility vehicle. Park like a storefront.

From street cart to micro-enterprise platform.

The same chassis could later support fruit sellers, flower vendors, tea carts, repair services, cold-box delivery, waste collection and other neighbourhood businesses.
